paras.en: "That is because the argument borders on frivolous."
paras.zh: “那是因为这种争论近乎无聊。”

paras.en: The judge noted that Comey was fired despite having had excellent performance reviews.
paras.zh: 法官指出，尽管科米表现出色，但他还是被解雇了。

paras.en: "Comey's supervisors and peers consistently lauded her work, describing her as a 'brilliant lawyer and a gifted supervisor,' 'the lawyer the office turns to when legal excellence is a must,' and 'an outstanding AUSA in every respect' with 'judgment, work product, and courtroom advocacy [that are] among the finest in the country,'" Furman wrote.
paras.zh: 弗曼写道：“科米的主管和同事一直称赞她的工作，形容她是一位‘才华横溢的律师和一位有天赋的主管’，‘当办公室需要卓越的法律能力时可以求助的律师’，‘在各个方面都是杰出的 AUSA’，‘判断力、工作成果和法庭辩护都是全国最好的’。”

paras.en: The DOJ admitted that Comey's termination "was not 'for cause' and was not based on her
paras.zh: 美国司法部承认，解雇科米“不是‘有原因’，也不是基于她

paras.en: In addition, the judge said, the DOJ's argument that Comey's termination was lawful ignored parts of the Civil Service Reform Act, which "required that Comey be given advance written notice (subject to certain exceptions not relevant here); 'a reasonable time' to respond orally and in writing; representation; and 'a written decision and the specific reasons therefor at the earliest practicable date.'"
paras.zh: 此外，法官表示，司法部认为科米的解雇合法性的论点忽略了《公务员制度改革法案》的部分内容，该法案“要求向科米发出提前书面通知（但与此处无关的某些例外情况除外）；口头和书面回应的‘合理时间’；陈述；以及‘尽早在可行日期做出书面决定及其具体原因。’”

paras.en: "Defendants concede, as they must, that Comey was not afforded these procedural protections," the judge said.
paras.zh: “被告承认，他们必须承认，科米没有获得这些程序保护，”法官说。

paras.en: Furman also said the DOJ all but admitted that its argument that the attorney general had power to fire Comey under Article II of the U.S. Constitution — which establishes the executive branch of government — sought "to overturn nearly two centuries of Supreme Court precedent."
paras.zh: 弗曼还表示，司法部几乎承认，其关于司法部长有权根据美国宪法第二条解雇科米的论点——该条建立了政府行政部门——试图“推翻最高法院近两个世纪的先例”。

paras.en: "This Court, however, is bound to follow the Supreme Court's precedents unless and until the Supreme Court overturns them," Furman wrote.
paras.zh: “然而，本法院必须遵循最高法院的先例，除非最高法院推翻这些先例，”弗曼写道。

paras.en: The DOJ, in a statement, said, "The Department disagrees with this decision and will appeal in due course."
paras.zh: 美国司法部在一份声明中表示，“该部门不同意这一决定，并将在适当时候提出上诉。”

paras.en: That appeal would happen after Furman issues a final judgment in the case.
paras.zh: 弗曼对此案作出最终判决后将提出上诉。

paras.en: The judge reserved judgment on Comey's claim that her firing violated her First Amendment rights. Furman gave her until Nov. 9 to file arguments on why that claim should not be dismissed as moot given his order in her favor on other grounds.
paras.zh: 法官保留对科米关于解雇她侵犯了她的第一修正案权利的主张的判决。弗曼要求她在 11 月 9 日之前提出论据，说明为什么这一主张不应被视为没有实际意义而被驳回，因为他以其他理由做出了对她有利的命令。

paras.en: CNBC has requested comment on the ruling from the White House.
paras.zh: CNBC 已要求白宫对这一裁决发表评论。

paras.en: Comey, in a note to colleagues at the U.S. Attorney's Office after she was fired, wrote, "If a career prosecutor can be fired without reason, fear may seep into the decisions of those who remain."
paras.zh: 科米在被解雇后给美国检察官办公室同事的一封信中写道：“如果一名职业检察官可以无故被解雇，那么恐惧可能会渗透到那些留下来的人的决定中。”

paras.en: "Fear is the tool of a tyrant, wielded to suppress independent thought. Instead of fear, let this moment fuel the fire that already burns in the heart of this place," she wrote. "A fire of righteous indignation at abuses of power. Of commitment to seek justice for victims."
paras.zh: “恐惧是暴君用来压制独立思想的工具。与其恐惧，不如让这一刻为这个地方的中心已经燃烧的火焰火上浇油，”她写道。 “对滥用权力的义愤之火。致力于为受害者寻求正义。”

articles.title: Snakes that cartwheel, vultures that groan, a mysterious Martian moon, and more

paras.en: Happy Monday, listeners! For Scientific American’s Science Quickly, I’m Rachel Feltman. You’re listening to our weekly science news roundup.
paras.zh: 听众们，星期一快乐！我是《科学美国人》的《科学快报》的雷切尔·费尔特曼。您正在收听我们的每周科学新闻综述。

paras.en: Let’s start with some space news. Last week, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, or JAXA for short, successfully launched a half-a-billion-dollar mission to land on Phobos, the largest Martian moon.
paras.zh: 让我们从一些太空新闻开始。上周，日本宇宙航空研究开发机构（简称 JAXA）成功启动了一项耗资 5 亿美元的任务，登陆火星最大的卫星火卫一。

paras.en: The Martian Moons Exploration spacecraft, also known as MMX, is expected to reach the vicinity of Mars in August of 2027. Once there, it will spend three years circling Mars in a path similar to Phobos’s orbit. One of its objectives is to find an ideal spot for landing on Phobos. In 2028 or 2029, MMX will send a rover down to the surface to spend 100 days observing the moon. That data will come in handy later in 2029, when MMX itself will attempt one or even two landings. If all goes well, MMX will return back up to orbit with 10 grams, or one-third of an ounce, of material from Phobos. It’s expected to make it back to Earth sometime in 2031.
paras.zh: 火星卫星探索航天器，也称为 MMX，预计将于 2027 年 8 月到达火星附近。到达那里后，它将花费三年时间沿着与火卫一轨道类似的路径绕火星运行。其目标之一是寻找在火卫一上着陆的理想地点。 2028年或2029年，MMX将发射月球车到月球表面，进行为期100天的月球观测。这些数据将在 2029 年晚些时候派上用场，届时 MMX 本身将尝试一次甚至两次着陆。如果一切顺利，MMX 将携带 10 克（即三分之一盎司）来自火卫一的物质返回轨道。预计它将于 2031 年的某个时候返回地球。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: So, why all this effort to check out a lumpy little moon? Phobos may be just 14 miles wide, but it’s got a lot to say. With an orbit of just over seven hours, it’s closer to its planet than any other moon in our solar system. That orbit is also gradually shrinking, bringing it on a slow-but-steady collision course with Mars.
paras.zh: 那么，为什么要费尽心思去观察一颗凹凸不平的小月亮呢？火卫一可能只有 14 英里宽，但它有很多东西要说。它的轨道只有七个多小时，它比太阳系中的任何其他卫星都更接近其行星。该轨道也在逐渐缩小，使其与火星进行缓慢但稳定的碰撞。

paras.en: Then there’s the unknown origin of Phobos and its little sibling, the Martian moon Deimos. Scientists aren’t sure whether these wee moons were once asteroids that got too close to Mars or if they formed from debris after something collided with the red planet. When the MMX sample comes home, researchers will compare its composition against Martian material and asteroids to try to solve that mystery.
paras.zh: 还有火卫一和它的小兄弟——火星卫星火卫二的起源不明。科学家们不确定这些小卫星是否曾经是距离火星太近的小行星，或者它们是否是由与红色行星相撞后的碎片形成的。当 MMX 样本带回家后，研究人员将其成分与火星物质和小行星进行比较，试图解开这个谜团。

paras.en: Speaking of weird little guys with adorably tiny orbits, our next story features a little snake that uses cartwheels as a strange evasive maneuver.
paras.zh: 说到奇怪的小家伙，它们的轨道小得可爱，我们的下一个故事是一条小蛇，它使用侧手翻作为一种奇怪的躲避动作。

paras.en: Now, I don’t know about you, but I find cartwheels hard enough with two arms and legs to support me. But apparently there are tiny little snakes that put my acrobatic attempts to shame with nary a limb in sight. Scientists first showcased this ability with the dwarf reed snake in 2023, but now they’ve identified that same cartwheeling behavior in two additional species of the same genus, Pseudorabdion. And what’s even better is that they caught the bizarre locomotion on video.
paras.zh: 现在，我不了解你的情况，但我发现侧手翻足够坚硬，有两条胳膊和两条腿可以支撑我。但显然有一些小蛇让我的杂技尝试蒙羞，看不到任何肢体。科学家于 2023 年首次在矮芦苇蛇身上展示了这种能力，但现在他们在同属的另外两个物种 Pseudorabdion 中发现了同样的侧手翻行为。更好的是他们在视频中捕捉到了这种奇怪的运动。

paras.en: The snakes start out by making a tight little curve, kind of like the letter “C,” with its head up top, facing the direction it wants to go, and something like the middle of its body touching the ground. Then it reels forward until its tail is the part touching the ground, which gives it the momentum to launch itself into the air. While it’s airborne, the snake twists around until it gets itself into the position of the starting point of the next roll, and it alternates which side of its body strikes the ground with each rotation. And did I mention these snakes are tiny and adorable? I’m definitely not doing the footage of their limbless leaping justice, so you really gotta check the video out for yourself. We’ll link to that in our show notes!
paras.zh: 蛇首先会画出一条紧密的小曲线，有点像字母“C”，头朝上，面向它想要走的方向，身体中部接触地面。然后它向前滚动，直到尾巴接触地面的部分，这给了它飞向空中的动力。当它在空中时，蛇会扭转，直到它进入下一次滚动的起点位置，并且每次旋转都会交替用身体的哪一侧接触地面。我有没有提到这些蛇又小又可爱？我绝对不会拍摄他们无肢跳跃正义的镜头，所以你真的必须亲自检查一下视频。我们将在演出笔记中链接到该内容！

paras.en: Those aren’t the only animal showoffs we saw making headlines last week. In a study published last Wednesday, researchers shared the surprisingly complex range of sounds made by birds not generally known for their gorgeous singing voices: vultures.
paras.zh: 这些并不是我们上周看到的唯一登上头条的动物表演。在上周三发表的一项研究中，研究人员分享了秃鹰发出的令人惊讶的复杂声音范围，这些鸟类通常不以华丽的歌声而闻名。

paras.en: When you think of a vulture, you probably picture a relatively solitary and silent bird, maybe like a few of them flying around in an ominous circle but not much more than that. But the thing is that some species are quite social—and, as it turns out, those more gregarious species can also be quite vocal. Rüppell’s vultures, which nest in colonies hundreds of birds strong, are known to follow a literal pecking order when it comes time to pick a carcass clean. Some experts think that social complexity fuels the evolution of complex communication. So, the set hierarchy that these vultures live by made scientists wonder how they might use sound to communicate.
paras.zh: 当你想到秃鹫时，你可能会想到一种相对孤独和沉默的鸟，也许就像其中一些在不祥的圆圈中飞来飞去，但仅此而已。但事实是，有些物种非常群居，而且事实证明，那些更群居的物种也可能非常善于发声。鲁佩尔兀鹫在数百只强大的鸟群中筑巢，众所周知，当需要将尸体拾取干净时，它们会遵循字面上的啄食顺序。一些专家认为，社会的复杂性推动了复杂沟通的发展。因此，这些秃鹰所遵循的固定等级制度让科学家们想知道它们如何使用声音进行交流。

paras.en: Researchers captured 150 hours of noise from two groups of vultures in captivity, which contained something like 2,500 calls. When they analyzed qualities like pitch and length, they were able to distinguish 16 distinct call types, which could be double the average for birds in general, based on previous research.
paras.zh: 研究人员捕获了两组圈养秃鹫 150 小时的噪音，其中包含大约 2,500 次叫声。当他们分析音高和长度等特征时，他们能够区分 16 种不同的叫声类型，根据之前的研究，这可能是一般鸟类平均叫声类型的两倍。

paras.en: If you’re wondering what those calls sound like, well lucky for you we have some examples. The study authors dubbed the most common call the “metallic groan,” and it generally came from birds who were on the receiving end of some kind of aggression. There were also specific brays that came from vultures trying to bully other birds for food, hisses made in response, hoarse mating groans, and special calls made by parents as they lovingly puked food into their babies’ mouths.
paras.zh: 如果您想知道这些调用听起来是什么样的，那么幸运的是，我们有一些示例。研究作者将最常见的叫声称为“金属呻吟”，它通常来自受到某种攻击的鸟类。还有秃鹰试图欺负其他鸟类获取食物时发出的特殊叫声、作为回应的嘶嘶声、沙哑的交配呻吟声，以及父母在充满爱意地将食物吐到婴儿嘴里时发出的特殊叫声。

paras.en: For our next story, you know those tabloid stories that show celebrities, like, grocery shopping and stuff with the headline “they’re just like us?” Well slap some Japanese macaques onto those glossy pages. Because according to a study published last week in Royal Society Open Science, these monkeys have a lot in common with humans when it comes to responding to disease outbreaks.
paras.zh: 对于我们的下一个故事，您知道那些展示名人的小报故事，例如杂货店购物之类的标题为“他们就像我们一样？”我们将一些日本猕猴拍到那些光滑的页面上。因为根据上周发表在《皇家学会开放科学》上的一项研究，这些猴子在应对疾病爆发方面与人类有很多共同点。

paras.en: Not unlike the human tendency to stock up on hand sanitizer and wipe down groceries in the wake of a pandemic, the researchers say, primates who have survived life-threatening disease outbreaks remain more cautious about potential food contamination than their peers. That’s especially interesting given the fact that, for a macaque, there’s no public health agency announcing where a deadly ailment has come from. But even with no empirical knowledge of disease transmission, like literally these guys do not have germ theory, this study suggests that a brush with contagion inspires habits that limit exposure to new bugs.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，与人类在大流行后储存洗手液和擦拭杂货的倾向不同，在危及生命的疾病爆发中幸存下来的灵长类动物仍然比同龄人对潜在的食物污染更加谨慎。这尤其有趣，因为对于猕猴来说，没有公共卫生机构宣布致命疾病的来源。但即使没有疾病传播的经验知识，就像字面上这些人没有细菌理论一样，这项研究表明，接触传染病会激发限制接触新细菌的习惯。

paras.en: The study looked at Japanese macaques at a primate sanctuary in southern Texas, where they’re grouped into several distinct enclosures. Three groups experienced an outbreak of simian retrovirus Type II, which can cause a sickness similar to AIDS, back in 2020. A fourth enclosure was completely spared, which provided a natural control group.
paras.zh: 这项研究观察了德克萨斯州南部一个灵长类动物保护区的日本猕猴，它们被分为几个不同的围栏。早在 2020 年，三组就经历了 II 型猿猴逆转录病毒的爆发，这种病毒会导致类似于艾滋病的疾病。第四组则完全幸免，这提供了一个自然对照组。

paras.en: To test how that experience impacted pathogen avoidance, the researchers offered macaques food from visibly clean surfaces as well as ones seemingly contaminated by monkey poop, though covered by epoxy to prevent any actual disease risk. Previous studies have shown that this species will avoid some food with fecal contamination, but will risk it all for a favorite treat like a peanut. And, indeed, in this new study, monkeys ate from a seemingly dirty surface in 79 percent of trials. But in the groups that had survived an outbreak, monkeys went for the poop food less than half of the time. Even individuals who had not personally been sick were less likely to risk contamination.
paras.zh: 为了测试这种经历如何影响病原体的回避，研究人员为猕猴提供了来自明显干净的表面以及看似被猴粪便污染的表面的食物，尽管这些表面被环氧树脂覆盖以防止任何实际的疾病风险。先前的研究表明，该物种会避免一些受粪便污染的食物，但会冒着一切风险去吃花生等最喜欢的食物。事实上，在这项新研究中，79% 的试验中猴子都在看似肮脏的表面上进食。但在疫情爆发后幸存下来的群体中，只有不到一半的猴子会去吃粪便食物。即使个人没有生病的人也不太可能受到感染。

paras.en: Simian retrovirus Type II doesn’t actually spread through food, but via scratches and bites. But we know that disgust and pathogen avoidance are complicated—and not always actually very useful—in humans, too.
paras.zh: II 型猿猴逆转录病毒实际上并不通过食物传播，而是通过抓伤和咬伤传播。但我们知道，厌恶和回避病原体对人类来说也很复杂，而且实际上并不总是很有用。

paras.en: We’ll wrap up with a story about the funnest little animals of them all: preschoolers. Researchers were curious about why people seem to think that kids are more creative than adults, despite scientific evidence showing the opposite. In a study published last week in PLOS One, they had 92 preschoolers and 70 adults tackle three creative tasks: spending eight minutes drawing freely on blank paper with colored pens and spending eight minutes inventing and drawing a made-up animal. The study subjects were all asked about how much they enjoyed those activities, how anxious the tasks made them feel, and how confident they felt about the quality of what they’d come up with. Then their results were evaluated by five people trained in a system for rating creative work.
paras.zh: 我们将以一个关于所有最有趣的小动物的故事来结束：学龄前儿童。研究人员很好奇为什么人们似乎认为孩子比成年人更有创造力，尽管科学证据表明事实恰恰相反。在 PLOS One 上周发表的一项研究中，他们让 92 名学龄前儿童和 70 名成年人完成了三项创造性任务：花八分钟用彩色笔在白纸上自由绘画，并花八分钟发明和画一只虚构的动物。研究对象都被问及他们有多喜欢这些活动，这些任务让他们感到有多焦虑，以及他们对自己的成果的质量有多大信心。然后，他们的结果由五名接受过创造性工作评级系统培训的人员进行评估。

paras.en: It turns out that, at least in this case, adults were objectively more creative than preschoolers, coming up with more original and effective ideas—but they also enjoyed themselves way less and felt worse about their work. So if you often find yourself wishing you could recapture the boundless creativity of your youth, maybe you should actually just work on your self-confidence. One time a lady in my ceramic studio looked at what I was making and said, “Wow, I wish I gave myself that much freedom.” And I have to tell you, at the time, it did not feel good. But now, I think I might have changed my mind.
paras.zh: 事实证明，至少在这种情况下，成年人客观上比学龄前儿童更有创造力，能提出更多原创和有效的想法，但他们也不太享受自己的乐趣，对自己的工作感觉更糟。因此，如果您经常发现自己希望能够重新获得年轻时的无限创造力，也许您实际上应该只努力增强自信。有一次，我的陶瓷工作室里的一位女士看着我正在制作的东西，说：“哇，我希望给自己那么多自由。”我必须告诉你，当时的感觉并不好。但现在，我想我可能改变了主意。

paras.en: That’s all for this week’s news roundup. We’ll be back on Wednesday to see how science is showing up in the midterm elections.
paras.zh: 这就是本周新闻综述的全部内容。我们将于周三回来看看科学在中期选举中如何表现。

paras.en: For Scientific American, this is Rachel Feltman. Have a great week!
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》的这位人物是雷切尔·费尔特曼 (Rachel Feltman)。祝你度过愉快的一周！

articles.title: What is trypophobia? Why some people's skin crawls when they see tiny holes

paras.en: Since childhood, clusters of circles have made me queasy—especially holes. Just thinking of honeycombs or lotus seed pods makes my stomach churn and skin crawl. My affliction has a name: trypophobia. By some estimates, trypophobia affects roughly one in six people. But its rise is sometimes put down to an online meme—an aversion to holes had a moment on the mid-2000s Internet. The condition is no joke, however: it can be debilitating, causing panic attacks and nausea—in extreme cases, people stop driving, miss work or avoid nature for fear of confronting upsetting stimuli.
paras.zh: 从孩提时代起，一簇簇的圆圈就让我感到恶心——尤其是洞。只要一想到蜂窝或莲子荚，我就会胃部翻腾，浑身起鸡皮疙瘩。我的痛苦有一个名字：密集恐惧症。据估计，密集恐惧症影响了大约六分之一的人。但它的兴起有时被归结为一种网络迷因——2000 年代中期的互联网上曾一度出现过对漏洞的厌恶。然而，这种情况可不是开玩笑：它可能会使人衰弱，导致恐慌和恶心——在极端情况下，人们会因为害怕面对令人不安的刺激而停止开车、旷工或回避大自然。

paras.en: Researchers first described trypophobia in a 2013 paper and argued that it may be a primitive fear response to venomous animals. Other, more recent theories include that it’s a disease-avoidance instinct that makes us recoil from anything resembling skin lesions or parasites, a form of cortical hyperexcitability where clusters of holes trigger a neural response—a visual equivalent to nails on a chalkboard—or simply a condition that caught on because it was a meme.
paras.zh: 研究人员在 2013 年的一篇论文中首次描述了密集恐惧症，并认为这可能是对有毒动物的原始恐惧反应。其他较新的理论包括，这是一种避免疾病的本能，使我们对任何类似皮肤损伤或寄生虫的东西感到退缩，这是一种皮质过度兴奋的形式，其中成群的孔会触发神经反应——视觉上相当于黑板上的钉子——或者只是一种因为它是模因而流行的情况。

paras.en: Now scientists may finally be closing in on an answer. Geoff Cole—the British scientist who originally pitched the evolutionary fear of venomous animals theory in 2013—recently looked back at the evidence and made a new conclusion. In a 2026 paper, Cole and his co-authors came down in favor of the disease-avoidance theory. Reviewing experiments that tested people’s reactions to triggering images, he concluded that trypophobia is primarily driven by disgust, not fear.
paras.zh: 现在科学家们可能终于接近答案了。英国科学家杰夫·科尔 (Geoff Cole) 最初在 2013 年提出了对有毒动物的进化恐惧理论，最近回顾了证据并得出了新的结论。在 2026 年发表的一篇论文中，科尔和他的合著者表示支持疾病避免理论。在回顾了测试人们对触发图像的反应的实验后，他得出结论，密集恐惧症主要是由厌恶而不是恐惧引起的。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “Disgust is the mechanism with which we can detect things which carry disease,” says Cole, a researcher at the University of Essex’s Center for Brain Science in England. “It’s clear that the evidence, when you stack it up, is more in favor of the disease-avoidance hypothesis.”
paras.zh: “厌恶是我们检测携带疾病的事物的机制，”英国埃塞克斯大学脑科学中心的研究员科尔说。 “很明显，当你把这些证据叠加起来时，你会发现更支持疾病避免假说。”

paras.en: In one experiment, for example, college students were shown trypophobic images, typical fear-inducing pictures—such as those of snakes and spiders—and control images. Participants’ pupils constricted more when they saw the trypophobic images than any of the others—a sign that the parasympathetic nervous system, which is linked to disgust, was activated. Fear, by contrast, is linked to the sympathetic nervous system, which dilates the pupils.
paras.zh: 例如，在一项实验中，向大学生展示了密集恐惧症图像、典型的引起恐惧的图像（例如蛇和蜘蛛的图像）以及对照图像。当参与者看到密集恐惧症图像时，他们的瞳孔比其他任何人都收缩得更多——这表明与厌恶相关的副交感神经系统被激活。相比之下，恐惧与交感神经系统有关，交感神经系统会放大瞳孔。

paras.en: Other research suggests trypophobic people find hole clusters as unpleasant as pictures of skin disease and that people with a history of skin problems may find hole clusters particularly uncomfortable to look at.
paras.zh: 其他研究表明，有密集恐惧症的人会发现孔群就像皮肤病的图片一样令人不快，而有皮肤病史的人可能会觉得孔群看起来特别不舒服。

paras.en: That’s not to say fear has no role in trypophobia. Last year a French-led team concluded that while disgust is the “dominant emotion” for trypophobes, “fear is also not negligible.”
paras.zh: 这并不是说恐惧与密集恐惧症无关。去年，一个法国领导的研究小组得出结论，虽然厌恶是密集恐惧症患者的“主要情绪”，但“恐惧也不容忽视”。

paras.en: To fully settle the question, scientists would need more “hard evidence,” says Christopher DiMattina, a psychology professor at Florida Gulf Coast University. For example, people could be put in an fMRI machine to track their brain activity, then be shown trypophobic and control images. Amygdala activation would suggest fear, while responses in the insular cortex would suggest disgust, he says.
paras.zh: 佛罗里达海湾海岸大学心理学教授克里斯托弗·迪马蒂纳说，为了彻底解决这个问题，科学家们需要更多“确凿的证据”。例如，人们可以被放入功能磁共振成像机器中来跟踪他们的大脑活动，然后显示密集恐惧症和控制图像。他说，杏仁核的激活表明恐惧，而岛叶皮层的反应则表明厌恶。

paras.en: Clinically, phobias are considered anxiety disorders, but some researchers believe that everyone is a little trypophobic. Some people, like me, are bothered by such images but can mostly ignore them. Trypophobia isn’t an official diagnosis—but someone with it could be diagnosed under the term specific phobia if they have severe reactions that interfere with their daily life, according to Kevin Chapman, a clinical psychologist and director of the Kentucky Center for Anxiety and Related Disorders.
paras.zh: 临床上，恐惧症被认为是焦虑症，但一些研究人员认为，每个人都有点密集恐惧症。有些人，比如我，会被这些图像困扰，但大多会忽略它们。密集恐惧症并不是官方的诊断，但临床心理学家、肯塔基州焦虑及相关疾病中心主任凯文·查普曼表示，如果患有密集恐惧症的人有严重的反应干扰了他们的日常生活，那么他们就可以被诊断为特定恐惧症。

paras.en: “You can technically be phobic of anything,” Chapman says. “There are certain phobias that load more with what we call disgust sensitivity, versus, say, anxiety sensitivity.”
paras.zh: “从技术上讲，你可以对任何事情感到恐惧，”查普曼说。 “某些恐惧症更多的是我们所说的厌恶敏感性，而不是焦虑敏感性。”

paras.en: There is little research on effective treatments for trypophobia, and scientists have called for more investment in potential therapies that target disgust. Most people with trypophobia are offered exposure therapy—a form of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) that aims to gradually desensitize someone to the phobic trigger by exposing them to low-level versions of it in controlled settings.
paras.zh: 关于密集恐惧症有效治疗的研究很少，科学家呼吁对针对厌恶的潜在疗法进行更多投资。大多数患有密集恐惧症的人都会接受暴露疗法，这是一种认知行为疗法（CBT），旨在通过在受控环境中让患者接触低水平的恐惧触发因素，逐渐使他们对恐惧触发因素变得不敏感。

paras.en: In a handful of published case reports, treatment, including CBT, seems to reduce people’s fear-related symptoms, but it hardly affects their disgust response. That could be because disgust is “generally more resistant to exposure than fear,” according to researchers at Macquarie University in Australia. Just as important as exposure, they argue, is counterconditioning, in which the upsetting stimulus is paired with something positive, such as a good experience or relaxation exercises.
paras.zh: 在一些已发表的病例报告中，包括 CBT 在内的治疗似乎可以减轻人们与恐惧相关的症状，但几乎不会影响他们的厌恶反应。澳大利亚麦考瑞大学的研究人员表示，这可能是因为厌恶“通常比恐惧更能抵抗暴露”。他们认为，与暴露同样重要的是反调节，即令人不安的刺激与积极的事物相结合，例如良好的经历或放松练习。

paras.en: The Australian team put that to the test in a small trial that aimed to alleviate both fear and disgust in nine trypophobic people. The participants underwent a one-session treatment that condensed key CBT principles into a single three-hour session—and was modified to include counterconditioning and other techniques to help them adjust their thinking. A month after the session, most participants reported significant improvements in both disgust and fear.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚团队在一项小型试验中对此进行了测试，旨在减轻九名密集恐惧症患者的恐惧和厌恶。参与者接受了一次治疗，将关键的 CBT 原则浓缩为一个三小时的治疗，并进行了修改，包括反调节和其他技术来帮助他们调整思维。课程结束一个月后，大多数参与者表示厌恶和恐惧都有显着改善。

paras.en: Chapman says treatment should be tailored to the trypophobic patient based on whether they experience more disgust, fear or anxiety. He recommends a combination of exposure therapy and cognitive restructuring, another CBT-based technique that aims to replace irrational thoughts with neutral, realistic alternatives.
paras.zh: 查普曼说，应该根据密集恐惧症患者是否感到更厌恶、恐惧或焦虑来制定治疗方案。他建议将暴露疗法和认知重建相结合，这是另一种基于 CBT 的技术，旨在用中立、现实的替代方案取代非理性想法。

paras.en: “Particularly when disgust sensitivity is high, you’ve got to really identify what they’re concerned would happen if they encounter it,” he says.
paras.zh: “特别是当厌恶敏感度很高时，你必须真正确定他们担心如果遇到这种情况会发生什么，”他说。

paras.en: If a person is worried about vomiting, for example, Chapman will work with them on applied muscle tension—a CBT-related technique—to tense up their core so they don’t actually puke. Applied tension is often used to help people with phobias related to needles or blood avoid fainting. Other individuals simply need help learning to tolerate the discomfort of seeing trypophobic images.
paras.zh: 例如，如果一个人担心呕吐，查普曼会与他们一起施加肌肉张力（一种与 CBT 相关的技术），以拉紧他们的核心，这样他们就不会真正呕吐。施加张力通常用于帮助患有针头或血液相关恐惧症的人避免晕厥。其他人只是需要帮助学习忍受看到密集恐惧症图像的不适。

paras.en: “Learning history does matter,” Chapman says.
paras.zh: “学习历史确实很重要，”查普曼说。

articles.title: How birds can quietly spread a severe form of pneumonia

paras.en: Birds are everywhere. They perch on rooftops and windowsills and sometimes share our homes as pets. But they can also carry dangerous germs, even when they appear healthy.
paras.zh: 鸟儿无处不在。它们栖息在屋顶和窗台上，有时作为宠物与我们同住。但它们也可能携带危险的细菌，即使它们看起来很健康。

paras.en: In a recent case report published in Frontiers in Medicine, a 43-year-old man presented with a persistent fever of 104 degrees Fahrenheit (40 degrees Celsius), fatigue and muscle pain but few respiratory symptoms. Several courses of antibiotics failed to bring down his fever.
paras.zh: 在《医学前沿》最近发表的一份病例报告中，一名 43 岁男性出现持续发烧 104 华氏度（40 摄氏度）、疲劳和肌肉疼痛，但几乎没有呼吸道症状。几个疗程的抗生素未能让他退烧。

paras.en: Doctors detected abnormal breath sounds, and a scan revealed a round blotch in his right lung—a sign of blood, pus, fluid or tissue—but tests for common pathogens came back negative. Suspecting a more unusual infection, they tested samples from his lungs and identified the culprit: Chlamydia psittaci, a bird-borne bacterium.
paras.zh: 医生检测到异常的呼吸音，扫描显示他的右肺有一个圆形斑点——这是血液、脓液、液体或组织的迹象——但常见病原体的检测结果呈阴性。由于怀疑存在更不寻常的感染，他们对他的肺部样本进行了检测，并确定了罪魁祸首：鹦鹉热衣原体，一种鸟传细菌。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The finding was key: the man switched antibiotics and recovered.
paras.zh: 这一发现很关键：该男子更换了抗生素并康复了。

paras.en: The likely source of the pathogen was a visit to a zoo, where the man had had direct contact with parrots about 10 days before his symptoms began. The infection, known as psittacosis, or parrot fever, can spread from many different birds, however, including poultry and pigeons.
paras.zh: 病原体的可能来源是该男子在出现症状前约 10 天曾去过动物园，在那里与鹦鹉有过直接接触。然而，这种被称为鹦鹉热或鹦鹉热的感染可以从许多不同的鸟类传播，包括家禽和鸽子。

paras.en: Another case report describes a 16-year-old boy who developed pneumonia from a C. psittaci infection after he cleaned his dormitory, including by dusting windowsills and ventilation systems—despite the fact that he had no known direct contact with birds.
paras.zh: 另一份病例报告描述了一名 16 岁男孩在打扫宿舍（包括除尘窗台和通风系统）后因鹦鹉热衣原体感染而患上肺炎，尽管事实上他没有与鸟类直接接触过。

paras.en: These cases show how everyday activities can expose people, sometimes unknowingly, to bird-borne diseases.
paras.zh: 这些案例表明，日常活动有时会使人们在不知不觉中接触到鸟传疾病。

paras.en: “Psittacosis is a respiratory disease mainly spread through inhaling the dust of bird droppings. You need to breathe in the bacteria to get infected,” says Brian Labus, an infectious disease epidemiologist at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas.
paras.zh: “鹦鹉热是一种呼吸道疾病，主要通过吸入鸟粪灰尘传播。你需要吸入细菌才会被感染，”拉斯维加斯内华达大学传染病流行病学家布莱恩·拉布斯说。

paras.en: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention states that there is no evidence that C. psittaci spreads through preparing or eating poultry products, though other case reports raise this possibility.
paras.zh: 美国疾病控制与预防中心表示，没有证据表明鹦鹉热衣原体通过制备或食用家禽产品传播，尽管其他病例报告提出了这种可能性。

paras.en: One, published in Case Reports in Infectious Diseases, described a chef who may have contracted psittacosis through handling poultry. Another, published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases, involved a man who developed fever and severe diarrhea after eating undercooked pigeon meat. The same bacterial strain was detected in the patient and in pigeons from the source of the meat, raising the possibility of foodborne transmission. But the exact routes of transmission in these cases remains unclear.
paras.zh: 其中一篇发表在《传染病病例报告》中，描述了一名厨师可能因处理家禽而感染了鹦鹉热病。另一篇发表在《国际传染病杂志》上的报道称，一名男子在食用未煮熟的鸽子肉后出现发烧和严重腹泻。在患者和来自肉类来源的鸽子中检测到相同的细菌菌株，增加了食源性传播的可能性。但这些病例的确切传播途径仍不清楚。

paras.en: Psittacosis can be difficult to recognize because its symptoms resemble those of other respiratory illnesses.
paras.zh: 鹦鹉热很难识别，因为它的症状与其他呼吸道疾病相似。

paras.en: “There are no unique symptoms that can make you suspect psittacosis as the cause of a respiratory illness, and doctors can’t tell without laboratory testing,” Labus says. He recommends that people with symptoms tell their doctor about any bird-related exposures, including caring for pet birds or cleaning up after wild birds.
paras.zh: 拉布斯说：“没有任何独特的症状可以让你怀疑鹦鹉热是呼吸系统疾病的原因，如果没有实验室测试，医生就无法判断。”他建议有症状的人告诉医生任何与鸟类有关的接触，包括照顾宠物鸟或清理野鸟。

paras.en: According to the CDC, fewer than 10 cases of parrot fever are typically reported in the U.S. each year. Psittacosis may be more common than reported figures suggest.
paras.zh: 据 CDC 称，美国每年报告的鹦鹉热病例通常不到 10 例。鹦鹉热可能比报告的数据显示的更常见。

paras.en: “Many infections probably go undiagnosed and are simply classified as community-acquired pneumonia without identifying the underlying causative pathogen,” says Daisy Vanrompay, a professor at Ghent University in Belgium. She directs the country’s national reference laboratory for human C. psittaci infections.
paras.zh: 比利时根特大学教授黛西·万隆佩 (Daisy Vanrompay) 表示：“许多感染可能未经诊断，只是被简单地归类为社区获得性肺炎，而没有确定潜在的致病病原体。”她领导该国人类鹦鹉热鹦鹉热感染国家参考实验室。

paras.en: While some infections are mild, others can cause severe pneumonia and, in rare cases, damage to organs such as the heart, liver and brain.
paras.zh: 虽然有些感染是轻微的，但其他感染可能会导致严重的肺炎，在极少数情况下，还会损害心脏、肝脏和大脑等器官。

paras.en: Severity depends on the amount of bacteria that’s inhaled, the strain that’s involved and individual susceptibility, Vanrompay says. Labus adds that young children, older adults and people with weakened immune systems or underlying lung conditions may be at greater risk of severe illness.
paras.zh: Vanrompay 说，严重程度取决于吸入的细菌数量、涉及的菌株以及个人的易感性。拉布斯补充说，幼儿、老年人和免疫系统较弱或有潜在肺部疾病的人患严重疾病的风险可能更大。

paras.en: To reduce exposure, both experts recommend wetting bird droppings before removal rather than dry sweeping or vacuuming them and wearing a well-fitting respirator when cleaning contaminated areas.
paras.zh: 为了减少接触，两位专家建议在清除鸟粪之前润湿鸟粪，而不是干扫或吸尘，并在清洁污染区域时佩戴合适的呼吸器。

articles.title: The human voice
articles.author: Nancy Shute

paras.en: Our voices have superpowers. From a coach firing up a soccer team before a big game to a mother soothing a cranky baby in the middle of the night, the human voice is key to expressing feelings and forging connections. The tone of a person’s voice might even communicate feelings to loved ones better than facial expressions. So what happens to a person when their voice disappears?
paras.zh: 我们的声音有超能力。从教练在一场重大比赛前激励足球队到母亲在半夜安抚脾气暴躁的婴儿，人声是表达感情和建立联系的关键。一个人的语气甚至可能比面部表情更能向亲人传达感情。那么当一个人的声音消失时会发生什么呢？

paras.en: People who have lost the ability to speak due to neurodegenerative disease or brain injury are talking again thanks to groundbreaking technologies that can decode the instructions the brain sends to speech muscles. For this issue’s cover story, senior neuroscience writer Laura Sanders interviewed Casey Harrell, a man who regained his voice — lost to ALS — through a brain-computer interface.
paras.zh: 由于神经退行性疾病或脑损伤而失去说话能力的人可以再次说话，这要归功于能够解码大脑发送到言语肌肉的指令的突破性技术。在本期封面故事中，资深神经科学作家劳拉·桑德斯 (Laura Sanders) 采访了凯西·哈勒尔 (Casey Harrell)，他因肌萎缩侧索硬化症 (ALS) 失去了声音，但通过脑机接口恢复了声音。

paras.en: You can listen to Harrell in his own words in Season Two of The Deep End, our award-winning podcast. Harrell told Sanders: “It was so amazing to be able to be understood right from the get-go and to be able to talk and respond to my daughter, especially because that was lacking completely from my life.”
paras.zh: 您可以在我们屡获殊荣的播客《The Deep End》第二季中聆听哈勒尔的自述。哈雷尔告诉桑德斯：“能够从一开始就被理解，能够与我的女儿交谈并做出回应，真是太棒了，尤其是因为我的生活完全缺乏这些。”

paras.en: In the podcast, Sanders digs into other innovations, including AI voice cloning, as well as the sinister potential of such technology to hijack people’s voices. “It might be used in a way people don’t want to have happen,” she says. Hear more wherever you get your podcasts.
paras.zh: 在播客中，桑德斯深入探讨了其他创新，包括人工智能语音克隆，以及此类技术劫持人们声音的险恶潜力。 “它可能会以人们不希望发生的方式被使用，”她说。无论您在何处获取播客，都能听到更多内容。

paras.en: In this issue, we also report on the progress in developing an effective treatment for stiff person syndrome, a rare autoimmune disorder that makes the body’s muscles freeze without warning. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration hasn’t yet approved any treatments for the disorder, which occurs in roughly 2 in 100,000 people. But that could some day change. Researchers are testing new CAR T cell therapies, senior writer Meghan Rosen reports. The process involves modifying a patient’s white blood cells so they wipe out harmful immune cells. Scientists hope a single treatment could cure the disease.
paras.zh: 在本期中，我们还报道了开发针对僵人综合症的有效治疗方法的进展，僵人综合症是一种罕见的自身免疫性疾病，会导致身体的肌肉在没有警告的情况下冻结。美国食品和药物管理局尚未批准任何治疗这种疾病的方法，这种疾病的发病率约为十万分之二。但有一天这种情况可能会改变。资深作家 Meghan Rosen 报道称，研究人员正在测试新的 CAR T 细胞疗法。该过程涉及修改患者的白细胞，从而消除有害的免疫细胞。科学家希望单一疗法就能治愈这种疾病。

paras.en: And there’s more controversy about using AI in mathematics, senior physics writer Emily Conover reports. OpenAI made waves when the company announced that it had solved one of the most famous puzzles in math — a day after mathematicians reported advances on a similar problem. The development is among a flood of AI-fueled achievements this year and raises big questions about who gets credit when the algorithms are doing the work.
paras.zh: 高级物理学作家艾米丽·科诺弗 (Emily Conover) 报道称，关于在数学中使用人工智能存在更多争议。当 OpenAI 宣布解决了数学界最著名的难题之一时，引起了轰动——一天前，数学家们报告了类似问题的进展。这一进展是今年人工智能推动的众多成就之一，并引发了一个大问题：当算法完成工作时，谁会获得功劳。

articles.title: Claude helped plan risky bird flu research. What did the AI add?
articles.author: Sascha Brodsky

paras.en: Anthropic’s Claude AI chatbot helped a scientist plan potentially risky bird flu experiments.
paras.zh: Anthropic 的 Claude AI 聊天机器人帮助一位科学家计划有潜在风险的禽流感实验。

paras.en: The researcher relied on Claude to plan studies, analyze data and choose experiments involving highly pathogenic avian influenza, the company reported September 10 in a threat intelligence report. The work sought to identify and introduce mutations that could help bird flu viruses adapt to mammals and transmit more easily between them. Anthropic says that, to its knowledge, no private company had previously publicly shared evidence of potential misuse of its platform for biological weapons development. But the company did not provide enough detail to determine whether Claude simply sped up work the researcher could already do or gave the researcher a new capability, experts say.
paras.zh: 该公司 9 月 10 日在一份威胁情报报告中称，研究人员依靠克劳德来规划研究、分析数据并选择涉及高致病性禽流感的实验。这项工作试图识别和引入突变，帮助禽流感病毒适应哺乳动物并更容易在它们之间传播。 Anthropic 表示，据其所知，此前没有任何私营公司公开分享过可能滥用其平台进行生物武器开发的证据。但专家表示，该公司没有提供足够的细节来确定克劳德是否只是加快了研究人员已经可以完成的工作，或者赋予了研究人员新的能力。

paras.en: Learning how avian influenza viruses might pose a pandemic risk “is absolutely a normal part of virology research,” says influenza researcher Thomas Friedrich of the University of Wisconsin–Madison School of Veterinary Medicine. Such research can help scientists assess whether emerging bird flu viruses pose a greater risk to humans.
paras.zh: 威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校兽医学院的流感研究员托马斯·弗里德里希（Thomas Friedrich）表示，了解禽流感病毒如何可能造成大流行风险“绝对是病毒学研究的正常组成部分”。此类研究可以帮助科学家评估新出现的禽流感病毒是否对人类构成更大的风险。

paras.en: But experiments that deliberately aim to boost pathogen traits such as transmissibility or disease severity draw scrutiny, Friedrich says, because of concerns about accidents or misuse.
paras.zh: 但弗里德里希说，出于对事故或滥用的担忧，故意旨在增强病原体特征（例如传播性或疾病严重程度）的实验受到了严格审查。

paras.en: Though the report comes amid broader debates about the security of AI models, arguments over this “gain-of-function” research predate generative AI. In 2012, studies involving H5N1 bird flu and airborne transmission in ferrets prompted an international debate over whether the scientific benefits outweighed the risks. Some H5N1 transmission experiments were put on hold for a year while researchers and officials worked out how to handle the risks.
paras.zh: 尽管该报告是在有关人工智能模型安全性的更广泛辩论中发布的，但有关“功能获得”研究的争论早于生成式人工智能。 2012年，涉及H5N1禽流感和雪貂空气传播的研究引发了一场关于科学效益是否大于风险的国际争论。一些 H5N1 传播实验被搁置一年，研究人员和官员正在研究如何应对风险。

paras.en: In Anthropic’s case, discovered in May 2026, the bird flu researcher accessed Claude from a region where the service was not supported or available. Anthropic says the researcher used workarounds to access Claude anyway. Material shared with Claude suggested the group probably had physical access to relevant virus samples. Anthropic banned the researcher’s account in May for evading restrictions on access.
paras.zh: 在 2026 年 5 月发现的 Anthropic 案例中，禽流感研究人员从不支持或不提供该服务的地区访问了 Claude。 Anthropic 表示，研究人员无论如何都使用了变通办法来访问克劳德。与克劳德分享的材料表明，该组织可能能够实际接触到相关病毒样本。 Anthropic 在 5 月份禁止了该研究人员的账户，因为该账户规避了访问限制。

paras.en: Anthropic says it could not tell whether the researcher intended harm because legitimate and dangerous biological research can look similar. The company did not respond to questions from Science News about why it considered the case significant, how it assessed Claude’s role in the research or whether any proposed experiments had actually been performed.
paras.zh: Anthropic 表示，它无法判断研究人员是否有意造成伤害，因为合法和危险的生物学研究可能看起来很相似。该公司没有回答《科学新闻》关于为何认为此案意义重大、如何评估克劳德在研究中的作用以及是否实际进行了任何拟议实验的问题。

paras.en: Anthropic released too little information to determine the purpose of the work, says biodefense researcher Gregory Koblentz. “There is no evidence that any of this research was connected to the development of biological weapons,” says Koblentz of George Mason University in Fairfax, Va.
paras.zh: 生物防御研究员格雷戈里·科布伦茨 (Gregory Koblentz) 表示，人类发布的信息太少，无法确定这项工作的目的。 “没有证据表明任何这项研究与生物武器的开发有关，”弗吉尼亚州费尔法克斯乔治梅森大学的科布伦茨说。

paras.en: The same kind of biological research can serve very different purposes, from civilian science to military defense. Even work done at a military-affiliated institution does not, on its own, show that researchers are developing a biological weapon, Koblentz says.
paras.zh: 同一种生物研究可以服务于从民用科学到军事防御等截然不同的目的。科布伦茨说，即使是在军事附属机构完成的工作本身也不能表明研究人员正在开发生物武器。

paras.en: Anthropic also did not provide enough detail to show exactly how much Claude helped, Friedrich says. The company’s own account suggests the AI model “did not meaningfully add scientific capability,” he says. In other words, it may simply have sped up the researcher’s work, rather than enabling something they could not have done otherwise.
paras.zh: 弗里德里希说，人性化也没有提供足够的细节来显示克劳德到底提供了多少帮助。他说，该公司自己的说法表明人工智能模型“并没有有意义地增加科学能力”。换句话说，它可能只是加快了研究人员的工作速度，而不是实现了他们本来无法完成的事情。

paras.en: Even if Claude’s role was only to speed up the work, that can make a big difference in a scientist’s workflow, says virologist David O’Connor of the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Systems such as Claude can help researchers find papers, synthesize results and parse data more quickly, he says. “Work or analyses that would have taken me months can now be done in an afternoon.”
paras.zh: 威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校的病毒学家大卫·奥康纳说，即使克劳德的作用只是加快工作速度，这也可以对科学家的工作流程产生很大的影响。他说，像克劳德这样的系统可以帮助研究人员更快地找到论文、综合结果和解析数据。 “原本需要花费几个月时间的工作或分析现在可以在一个下午完成。”

paras.en: As a result, existing scientific information, including about avian flu viruses, may become easier to find and use, O’Connor says. O’Connor says frontier AI models could let scientists tackle questions they might not have attempted before. “The frontier models will change the ambition of research questions that are asked,” he says.
paras.zh: 奥康纳说，因此，现有的科学信息，包括有关禽流感病毒的信息，可能会变得更容易找到和使用。奥康纳表示，前沿人工智能模型可以让科学家解决他们以前可能没有尝试过的问题。 “前沿模型将改变所提出的研究问题的雄心，”他说。

paras.en: The bird flu research was one of five instances in Anthropic’s report involving uses of Claude that the company says could support biological weapons development. None of the five look technically sophisticated or particularly concerning to biologist Kevin Esvelt of the MIT Media Lab. Esvelt is more suspicious of the researchers’ motives; he says the five cases showed signs of ill intent. But none “represented a competent attempt at weaponization.”
paras.zh: 禽流感研究是 Anthropic 报告中涉及使用克劳德的五个实例之一，该公司称这些实例可以支持生物武器的开发。对于麻省理工学院媒体实验室的生物学家凯文·埃斯维尔特来说，这五者中没有一个看起来技术复杂或特别令人担忧。艾斯维特对研究人员的动机更加怀疑。他说，这五起案件显示出恶意的迹象。但没有一个“代表了武器化的有力尝试”。

paras.en: The poor quality of these particular attempts does not show what a more capable user might be able to do with AI-assisted biology, Esvelt says. AI can help with research and analysis, but turning an idea into a biological threat takes additional work, Koblentz says. “Even if AI is used to design a potentially dangerous pathogen, it is not a threat until the organism can be modified in a lab or synthesized.”
paras.zh: Esvelt 说，这些特定尝试的质量较差，并不能表明更有能力的用户可以利用人工智能辅助生物学做些什么。科布伦茨说，人工智能可以帮助研究和分析，但将一个想法转化为生物威胁需要额外的工作。 “即使人工智能被用来设计一种潜在危险的病原体，它也不会构成威胁，除非该生物体可以在实验室中进行修改或合成。”

paras.en: That requires facilities, measures for keeping viruses contained, funding, trained personnel and hands-on experience. Those barriers vary depending on who is doing the work, O’Connor says. They would be a major obstacle for an inexperienced person working alone, but less so for scientists with specialized training and access to a well-equipped laboratory.
paras.zh: 这需要控制病毒的设施、措施、资金、训练有素的人员和实践经验。奥康纳说，这些障碍取决于谁在做这项工作。对于缺乏经验的单独工作的人来说，它们将是一个主要障碍，但对于接受过专门培训并可以进入设备齐全的实验室的科学家来说，情况就不那么严重了。

paras.en: Regardless, the remaining laboratory steps are substantial, Friedrich writes in an email. “There is a big gap between identifying mutations that could potentially adapt an avian influenza virus to humans and a ‘harmful biological outcome’.”
paras.zh: 无论如何，剩下的实验室步骤是实质性的，弗里德里希在一封电子邮件中写道。 “识别可能使禽流感病毒适应人类的突变与‘有害的生物学结果’之间存在很大差距。”

articles.title: Volcanoes lurk behind the scenes of human history
articles.author: Carolyn Wilke

paras.en: “The bright sun was extinguish’d … and the icy earth swung blind and blackening in the moonless air.” These words from Lord Byron’s 1816 poem Darkness evoke a hellish apocalypse. But Byron may have been inspired by the fallout of a real cataclysm — one that happened half a world away.
paras.zh: “明亮的太阳熄灭了……冰冷的大地在无月的空气中变得盲目、变黑。”拜伦勋爵 1816 年的诗《黑暗》中的这些话唤起了地狱般的启示录。但拜伦的灵感可能是来自一场真正的灾难——一场发生在半个世界之外的灾难。

paras.en: Mount Tambora, in present-day Indonesia, blew its top in 1815. More than 71,000 people in the vicinity died. And climate-cooling aerosols from the eruption ushered in extreme weather the following years in far-flung places. Cold weather in the summer of 1816, sometimes with frosts and snow, destroyed corn in New England, rice and buckwheat in China and wheat, oats and potatoes in Ireland. In some places, the rising cost of bread sparked protests and riots. The circumstances may have helped spread typhus. Some called 1816 “the year without a summer,” others “the year of the beggars.”
paras.zh: 坦博拉山（位于今印度尼西亚）于 1815 年发生火山喷发，导致附近地区 71,000 多人死亡。火山喷发产生的气候冷却气溶胶在接下来的几年里在偏远地区迎来了极端天气。 1816 年夏季的寒冷天气，有时还伴有霜冻和降雪，毁坏了新英格兰的玉米、中国的稻米和荞麦以及爱尔兰的小麦、燕麦和土豆。在一些地方，面包价格上涨引发了抗议和骚乱。这种情况可能有助于斑疹伤寒的传播。有人称 1816 年为“没有夏天的一年”，也有人称 1816 年为“乞丐之年”。

paras.en: Like Tambora, volcanoes, and the cooling they cause, may be an underappreciated geologic force at times moving behind the scenes of human history.
paras.zh: 与坦博拉一样，火山及其引起的降温有时可能是一种未被充分认识的地质力量，在人类历史的幕后活动。

paras.en: “These climatic impacts of the Tambora eruption were recorded without any knowledge that this had anything to do with an eruption,” says Clive Oppenheimer, a volcanologist at the University of Cambridge.
paras.zh: 剑桥大学火山学家克莱夫·奥本海默 (Clive Oppenheimer) 表示：“记录坦博拉火山喷发对气候的影响时，我们并不知道这与火山喷发有关。”

paras.en: While Tambora is the most well-studied eruption in history, others have also rattled the planet. Oppenheimer and his colleagues analyzed 38 large eruptions in the 2026 Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences. Their work pulled together studies linking the geologic events and their effects on climate with their potential societal fallout in food systems, the economy, unrest, culture and religion. The locations and exact timing of the eruptions that spurred some notable cold spurts aren’t known. But understanding how the events impacted the climate, environment and society can offer clues to the past, including how people coped with climate stress.
paras.zh: 虽然坦博拉火山喷发是历史上研究最深入的一次，但其他火山喷发也曾让地球感到不安。奥本海默和他的同事在《2026 年地球与行星科学年度评论》中分析了 38 次大型火山喷发。他们的工作汇集了将地质事件及其对气候的影响与粮食系统、经济、动乱、文化和宗教等潜在社会影响联系起来的研究。引发一些明显冷喷发的火山喷发的地点和确切时间尚不清楚。但了解这些事件如何影响气候、环境和社会可以为过去提供线索，包括人们如何应对气候压力。

paras.en: “Volcanic eruptions, they are kind of this like hammer blow to the climate system,” says Heli Huhtamaa, a climate and environmental historian at the University of Bern in Switzerland. Volcanoes may offer lessons about resilience for modern societies in a warming world, she says.
paras.zh: 瑞士伯尔尼大学气候和环境历史学家赫利·胡塔玛 (Heli Huhtamaa) 表示：“火山喷发就像是对气候系统的重击。”她说，火山可能为现代社会在变暖的世界中的恢复能力提供教训。

paras.en: Volcanoes spew sulfur-containing gases. Over weeks, those gases react in the atmosphere to form particles that block sunlight. The particles can stay aloft for many months, riding jet streams to encircle the globe. Paintings from years after eruptions show bloodred sunsets or landscapes shrouded by hazy skies.
paras.zh: 火山喷出含硫气体。几周后，这些气体在大气中发生反应，形成阻挡阳光的颗粒。这些粒子可以在高空停留数月，乘着急流环绕地球。火山喷发多年后的画作展示了血红色的日落或被朦胧的天空笼罩的风景。

paras.en: Because no two eruptions are exactly alike, it takes work to grasp each one’s impacts on weather and climate. “If we understand the climate response of one [eruption], that does not mean that we understand the climate response of another,” says Ulf Büntgen, a paleoclimatologist at the University of Cambridge.
paras.zh: 由于没有两次喷发是完全相同的，因此需要努力了解每次喷发对天气和气候的影响。剑桥大学古气候学家 Ulf Büntgen 表示：“如果我们了解一次[喷发]的气候反应，并不意味着我们了解另一次喷发的气候反应。”

paras.en: A volcano’s explosivity impacts how high it shoots its gases and where they travel. Over time, those gases form particles that block sunlight. The particles can stay aloft for many months, riding jet streams to encircle the globe. In this computer model of a 1991 eruption, colors represent how high particles are in the atmosphere. Red is high and blue is closer to Earth’s surface.
paras.zh: 火山的爆发力会影响其喷出气体的高度以及气体的传播位置。随着时间的推移，这些气体会形成阻挡阳光的颗粒。这些粒子可以在高空停留数月，乘着急流环绕地球。在这个 1991 年火山喷发的计算机模型中，颜色代表了大气中粒子的高度。红色较高，蓝色较接近地球表面。

paras.en: Researchers find the traces of past eruptions in ice cores from Greenland and Antarctica. Scientists try to nail down the date on a sulfur-loaded ice core layer and compare it with tree ring data, a logbook of sorts for summer growing conditions since temperatures impact how trees lay down their wood each year. Scientists can pull together tree ring records from far-flung places and use statistics to work out annual temperatures in a hemisphere.
paras.zh: 研究人员在格陵兰岛和南极洲的冰芯中发现了过去喷发的痕迹。科学家们试图确定含硫冰芯层上的日期，并将其与树木年轮数据进行比较，树木年轮数据是夏季生长条件的日志，因为温度会影响树木每年放下木材的方式。科学家可以收集遥远地方的树木年轮记录，并利用统计数据计算出半球的年气温。

paras.en: Cold spells sometimes jump out from tree ring records. For years when cool summers impeded the final stages of wood formation, a chemical method used to estimate temperatures turns wood layers blue. Büntgen and colleagues saw two blue rings around 1345. “And that is very rare. We never saw that two years in a row,” he says. The rings coincided with the timing of the Black Death’s spread in Europe, the team reported in 2025 in Communications Earth & Environment. The researchers traced the connections between chilly summers, poor grain harvests in the Mediterranean and shipping records showing how Italian city states imported flea-ridden grain from the Caucasus.
paras.zh: 寒潮有时会从树木年轮记录中跳出来。多年来，凉爽的夏季阻碍了木材形成的最后阶段，用于估算温度的化学方法使木层变成蓝色。 Büntgen 和同事在 1345 年左右看到了两个蓝色环。“这非常罕见。我们从未连续两年看到过这种情况，”他说。研究小组于 2025 年在《通信地球与环境》杂志上报告称，这些光环与黑死病在欧洲传播的时间一致。研究人员追踪了寒冷的夏季、地中海粮食歉收和意大利城邦如何从高加索地区进口跳蚤肆虐的谷物的航运记录之间的联系。

paras.en: Oppenheimer, Büntgen and their colleagues broadened the detective work for their 2026 review. The team studied Northern Hemisphere temperature responses to the 38 largest eruptions between A.D. 1 and 1900. On average, each volcano caused about 0.5 degrees Celsius of cooling in the year after the eruption. Recovery to normal temperatures was slower for eruptions that occurred in times that were already colder on average, Büntgen says. In some periods, large or successive eruptions may lead to an elevated amounts of particles in the atmosphere for a long time. The team’s calculations show that high aerosol levels concur with some of the past two millennia’s coldest spells, such as the one preceding the Black Death.
paras.zh: 奥本海默、邦特根和他们的同事扩大了 2026 年审查的侦探工作范围。研究小组研究了北半球对公元 1 年至 1900 年间 38 次最大火山喷发的温度反应。平均而言，每座火山在喷发后的一年内造成约 0.5 摄氏度的降温。宾根说，对于平均已经较冷的时期发生的火山喷发，恢复到正常温度的速度较慢。在某些时期，大规模或连续的喷发可能会导致大气中颗粒物的数量长期增加。研究小组的计算表明，高气溶胶水平与过去两千年来一些最冷的时期一致，例如黑死病之前的那一次。

paras.en: Human agency factors into eruptions’ outcomes
paras.zh: 人类因素影响火山喷发的结果

paras.en: Those cold snaps often had dire consequences. Out of 17 large-scale famines in Europe from 1300 to 1800, 11 followed major eruptions. In addition to faltering crops and famines, the most frequently societal responses described in studies collected by the review authors were disease outbreaks, political turmoil and migration.
paras.zh: 这些寒潮往往会带来可怕的后果。 1300年至1800年间，欧洲发生了17次大规模饥荒，其中11次是在大规模火山爆发之后发生的。除了农作物歉收和饥荒之外，该综述作者收集的研究中描述的最常见的社会反应是疾病爆发、政治动荡和移民。

paras.en: The societal circumstances surrounding eruptions are as important as the amount of cooling, Huhtamaa says. She and her colleagues studied crop failures and farmstead desertion in three different volcanic eruptions that impacted Ostrobothnia, in what is now Finland. During the 17th century, Ostrobothnia experienced cooling from three sets of eruptions at different time periods.
paras.zh: 胡塔玛说，围绕火山喷发的社会环境与降温程度同样重要。她和她的同事研究了影响博滕区（位于现在的芬兰）的三场不同火山喷发中的农作物歉收和农田荒废。 17 世纪，博滕区经历了不同时期的三轮喷发导致的降温。

paras.en: Although the latest eruption event, in 1695, was the coldest of all, peasants fared better than they had after eruptions earlier in the century, Huhtamaa and colleagues reported in 2022 in Climate of the Past. Though people still starved, only around 7 percent of peasants lost their farmland, compared with 20 percent in the other periods. This was because the crown provided tax relief, Huhtamaa says. This wasn’t humanitarian aid, as it was meant to preserve the tax base and prevent possibly decades of lost revenue.
paras.zh: Huhtamaa 及其同事在 2022 年的《过去的气候》中报告说，尽管 1695 年的最近一次火山喷发是所有火山中最冷的一次，但农民的情况比本世纪初火山喷发后的情况要好。尽管人们仍然在挨饿，但只有约 7% 的农民失去了耕地，而其他时期这一比例为 20%。胡塔玛说，这是因为政府提供税收减免。这不是人道主义援助，因为它的目的是保护税基并防止可能数十年的收入损失。

paras.en: “When there is a climatic shock, it doesn’t matter if it’s 0.5 or 1.5 degrees cooler, because what really matters is the societal vulnerability,” Huhtamaa says.
paras.zh: “当发生气候冲击时，气温降低 0.5 度还是 1.5 度并不重要，因为真正重要的是社会脆弱性，”Huhtamaa 说。

paras.en: Studies like Huhtamaa’s reveal how societies can tick on in spite of climate disasters. But historians haven’t always been keen to look to climate for clues to explain history. Human agency has often been considered the only reasonable explanation for human affairs, Huhtamaa says. “And climate explanations sounded lazy.”
paras.zh: 像胡塔玛这样的研究揭示了社会如何在气候灾难的影响下继续发展。但历史学家并不总是热衷于从气候中寻找解释历史的线索。胡塔玛说，人类能动性通常被认为是对人类事务的唯一合理解释。 “气候解释听起来很懒。”

paras.en: Investigating societies’ preconditions and responses to the climate change caused by volcanoes could help people prepare for a now warming world. A recent report from the United Nations’ Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, noted that not enough research had been done on responses, Huhtamaa says. Researchers could examine one place’s response to different events, as in Huhtamaa’s work on Ostrobothnia, or parse different locales’ responses to the same event. Meanwhile, greater use of insights from ecology, agronomy and economics, for instance, can help with this detective work that reveals how humans respond to climatic events beyond their control.
paras.zh: 研究社会对火山引起的气候变化的先决条件和应对措施可以帮助人们为现在变暖的世界做好准备。胡塔玛说，联合国政府间气候变化专门委员会最近的一份报告指出，尚未对应对措施进行足够的研究。研究人员可以检查一个地方对不同事件的反应，就像 Huhtamaa 对 Ostrobothnia 的研究一样，或者解析不同地区对同一事件的反应。与此同时，更多地利用生态学、农学和经济学等领域的见解，可以帮助开展这项侦探工作，揭示人类如何应对超出其控制的气候事件。

paras.en: Those responses appear in religion, too. For instance, lines in the famed 10th century poem Vǫluspá seem to reference the 939 eruption of Iceland’s Eldgjá volcano, with high-flying flames and blackened sun beams. “It’s like an eyewitness description of a phenomenal lava flood,” Oppenheimer says. The poem foretells a fiery end to pagan gods, such as Odin, who are replaced by one god. Vǫluspá, which explained the eruption in terms of divine displeasure,may have contributed to the island’s Christianization around 1000, Oppenheimer and colleagues suggest.
paras.zh: 这些反应也出现在宗教中。例如，著名的 10 世纪诗歌《Vǫluspá》中的诗句似乎参考了 939 年冰岛 Eldgja 火山的喷发，当时喷发的火焰高高飘扬，太阳光线变黑。 “这就像目击者对一场惊人的熔岩洪水的描述，”奥本海默说。这首诗预言了奥丁等异教诸神的惨烈结局，他们被一位神所取代。奥本海默及其同事认为，Vǫluspá 将火山喷发解释为神圣的不满，这可能促成了公元 1000 年左右该岛的基督教化。

paras.en: Famines, riots, disease, migration. The widespread climatic effects of volcanoes across the ages may be subtler than the hellscapes conjured by poets but more tangible in the marks they’ve left on history.
paras.zh: 饥荒、骚乱、疾病、移民。各个时代火山对气候的广泛影响可能比诗人想象中的地狱景象更微妙，但它们在历史上留下的印记却更为明显。

articles.title: Testosterone May Have an Unexpected Benefit For Women's Bones After Menopause
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Testosterone has historically been considered a 'male' sex hormone, but that outdated notion may be preventing better treatments for post menopausal women.
paras.zh: 睾酮历来被认为是一种“男性”性激素，但这种过时的观念可能阻碍了对绝经后女性更好的治疗。

paras.en: Along with estrogen, the ovaries also produce testosterone, and this overlooked androgen could be part of the reason why bone is lost in older age.
paras.zh: 除了雌激素之外，卵巢还产生睾酮，这种被忽视的雄激素可能是老年骨质流失的部分原因。

paras.en: A small new study has found that adding testosterone to hormone replacement therapy may protect bone density more than estrogen on its own.
paras.zh: 一项小型新研究发现，在激素替代疗法中添加睾酮可能比单独使用雌激素更能保护骨密度。

paras.en: The findings are not yet published in a peer-reviewed paper, but they were presented at the 2026 Annual Meeting of The Menopause Society in San Diego this October.
paras.zh: 研究结果尚未在同行评审论文中发表，但已于今年 10 月在圣地亚哥举行的更年期协会 2026 年年会上发表。

paras.en: "Menopausal patients deserve treatment options that reflect the complexity of their health needs, including long-term bone health," says lead author Sona Davis from the University of Southern California.
paras.zh: “更年期患者应该选择反映其健康需求复杂性的治疗方案，包括长期骨骼健康，”南加州大学的主要作者索娜·戴维斯说。

paras.en: "We hope that our findings can encourage further research into how testosterone could be used safely and effectively as part of individualized menopausal care."
paras.zh: “我们希望我们的发现能够鼓励进一步研究如何安全有效地使用睾酮作为个体化更年期护理的一部分。”

paras.en: Today, testosterone replacement therapy is best established as a bone treatment for men with low testosterone levels.
paras.zh: 如今，睾酮替代疗法最适合作为睾酮水平低的男性的骨骼治疗方法。

paras.en: But preliminary evidence suggests this therapy may work for women, too.
paras.zh: 但初步证据表明这种疗法也可能对女性有效。

paras.en: Estrogen levels are usually named as the main culprit for bone loss in women, but they may not act alone.
paras.zh: 雌激素水平通常被认为是女性骨质流失的主要原因，但它们可能不会单独起作用。

paras.en: After menopause, when menstruation ceases, estrogen levels are known to drop rapidly, and this is a major cause of weak, porous bones in older age.
paras.zh: 绝经后，当月经停止时，雌激素水平会迅速下降，这是老年人骨骼脆弱、多孔的主要原因。

paras.en: For decades now, estrogen therapy has been used to protect against bone loss in some older patients.
paras.zh: 几十年来，雌激素疗法一直被用来防止一些老年患者骨质流失。

paras.en: Replacing this hormone can increase bone density and reduce fractures in both the spine and the hip in postmenopausal women.
paras.zh: 替代这种激素可以增加绝经后女性的骨密度并减少脊柱和髋部骨折。

paras.en: But testosterone can also decrease with age, and recent studies have found evidence that it is linked to bone health, not just in older men but in women, too.
paras.zh: 但睾酮也会随着年龄的增长而减少，最近的研究发现有证据表明它与骨骼健康有关，不仅对老年男性如此，对女性也如此。

paras.en: In 2022, for instance, a population-based study among females aged 40 to 60 years in the US found that testosterone levels were positively associated with bone mineral density in the lumbar spine.
paras.zh: 例如， 2022年，一项针对美国40至60岁女性的人群研究发现，睾酮水平与腰椎骨密度呈正相关。

paras.en: "According to the literature, it is basically clear that testosterone promotes bone mineral density in males," the authors wrote at the time.
paras.zh: “根据文献，基本上很清楚睾酮可以促进男性的骨矿物质密度，”作者当时写道。

paras.en: But by contrast, the researchers said, evidence for females is "sparse and controversial."
paras.zh: 但研究人员表示，相比之下，针对女性的证据“很少且有争议”。

paras.en: To see if testosterone can improve estrogen therapy's benefits for women's bones, this new study analyzed the health outcomes of 51 postmenopausal participants.
paras.zh: 为了了解睾酮是否可以改善雌激素疗法对女性骨骼的益处，这项新研究分析了 51 名绝经后参与者的健康结果。

paras.en: These individuals were each prescribed hormone therapy at the same private hospital.
paras.zh: 这些人都在同一家私立医院接受了激素治疗。

paras.en: All the participants tried two therapies, each for at least a year, and typically for several years. One involved just estrogen, and the other involved both estrogen and testosterone.
paras.zh: 所有参与者都尝试了两种疗法，每种疗法至少一年，通常持续数年。一种只涉及雌激素，另一种涉及雌激素和睾酮。

paras.en: X-ray scans measured their bone mineral density at the start of the trial, and then again, one year into each type of therapy.
paras.zh: X射线扫描在试验开始时测量了他们的骨矿物质密度，然后在每种治疗一年后再次测量。

paras.en: Surprisingly, researchers found that estrogen therapy alone kept bone density stable, but didn't significantly increase it at any of the locations examined: not the lumbar spine, the femoral neck, or the hip.
paras.zh: 令人惊讶的是，研究人员发现，单独使用雌激素疗法可以保持骨密度稳定，但并没有显着增加任何检查部位的骨密度：腰椎、股骨颈或髋部都没有。

paras.en: But estrogen plus testosterone therapy did increase bone density scores for the lumbar spine.
paras.zh: 但雌激素加睾酮治疗确实增加了腰椎的骨密度评分。

paras.en: "These findings suggest that testosterone may exert a synergistic effect with estrogen on trabecular bone, particularly at the spine, and may offer enhanced skeletal benefit beyond estrogen alone," the authors conclude in an abstract supplied for the recent conference.
paras.zh: “这些发现表明，睾酮可能与雌激素对骨小梁发挥协同作用，特别是在脊柱上，并且可能比单独使用雌激素更能增强骨骼益处，”作者在最近会议提供的摘要中总结道。

paras.en: It's unclear whether these changes in spinal density are sufficient to reduce fracture risk, which is the main measure of success in osteoporosis treatment.
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚脊柱密度的这些变化是否足以降低骨折风险，而骨折风险是骨质疏松症治疗成功的主要衡量标准。

paras.en: But the results support the idea that testosterone may have a role to play in protecting bone health as we age.
paras.zh: 但结果支持这样的观点：随着年龄的增长，睾酮可能在保护骨骼健康方面发挥作用。

paras.en: In 2023, researchers at Monash University in Australia launched a trial to test this, noting that "there is some evidence that the addition of testosterone to estrogen replacement therapy might prevent bone loss and restore sexual function in women with early menopause."
paras.zh: 2023年，澳大利亚莫纳什大学的研究人员发起了一项试验来测试这一点，并指出“有一些证据表明，在雌激素替代疗法中添加睾酮可能会防止绝经早期女性的骨质流失并恢复性功能。”

paras.en: That same year, a small trial found that testosterone therapy alone or in combination with low-dose estrogen therapy can improve spine and hip bone density.
paras.zh: 同年，一项小型试验发现，单独使用睾酮疗法或与低剂量雌激素疗法相结合可以改善脊柱和髋部骨密度。

paras.en: But larger and longer trials are still needed, and these studies need to demonstrate reductions in fracture risk, not just increases in bone density.
paras.zh: 但仍需要更大规模、更长时间的试验，这些研究需要证明骨折风险的降低，而不仅仅是骨密度的增加。

paras.en: Knowing these clinical outcomes is key to evaluating the risks and benefits of hormone replacement therapy, which should be carefully weighed by clinicians and patients.
paras.zh: 了解这些临床结果是评估激素替代疗法的风险和益处的关键，临床医生和患者应仔细权衡。

paras.en: For now, it's important to recognize that testosterone is an essential hormone for the female body, impacting everything from the brain to the heart.
paras.zh: 目前，重要的是要认识到睾酮是女性身体的一种重要激素，影响从大脑到心脏的各个方面。

paras.en: How it affects our bones is a mystery we are only just starting to crack.
paras.zh: 它如何影响我们的骨骼是一个我们才刚刚开始破解的谜团。

articles.title: Global Warming Has Nearly Doubled in Speed Since 2010, Major Report Finds
articles.author: Russell McLendon

paras.en: The future we've feared is already here. In a new report, researchers detail how grim the climate crisis has become in 2026, and how Earth's climate system continues to plunge farther and faster into terrible new territory.
paras.zh: 我们所担心的未来已经到来。在一份新报告中，研究人员详细介绍了 2026 年气候危机变得多么严峻，以及地球气候系统如何继续更快更远地陷入可怕的新领域。

paras.en: "Rapid destabilization is now a diagnosis rather than a warning for the future," says co-lead author William Ripple, an ecologist at the Oregon State University College of Forestry.
paras.zh: “快速的不稳定现在是一种诊断，而不是对未来的警告，”共同主要作者、俄勒冈州立大学林业学院的生态学家威廉·里普尔说。

paras.en: Climate change can still get even worse, of course, and humanity still has cards to play. The report notes "important signs of societal and technological transformation are also emerging," albeit not quickly or broadly enough.
paras.zh: 当然，气候变化仍然可能变得更糟，而人类仍然有牌可打。报告指出，“社会和技术变革的重要迹象也正在出现”，尽管速度不够快，范围也不够广。

paras.en: "The accelerating expansion of renewable energy and advances in battery storage are encouraging, but they are only part of the transformation needed to stabilize the climate system," Ripple says.
paras.zh: “可再生能源的加速扩张和电池存储的进步令人鼓舞，但它们只是稳定气候系统所需的转型的一部分，”里普尔说。

paras.en: "A more resilient and sustainable future depends heavily on big cuts in greenhouse gas emissions, effective adaptation, and ecosystem protection."
paras.zh: “更具弹性和可持续的未来在很大程度上取决于温室气体排放的大幅削减、有效的适​​应和生态系统保护。”

paras.en: The report comes from an international coalition of climate scientists, marking the seventh annual update in the researchers' "state of the climate" series.
paras.zh: 该报告来自国际气候科学家联盟，标志着研究人员“气候状况”系列的第七次年度更新。

paras.en: The goal is to illuminate key vital signs of Earth along with human activities that affect them, the authors explain, but also to provide context and guidance.
paras.zh: 作者解释说，其目标是阐明地球的关键生命体征以及影响这些生命体征的人类活动，同时也提供背景和指导。

paras.en: "Documenting change is no longer enough," they write. "We must also communicate what it means and what actions are needed. As scientists, we have a responsibility to communicate these realities with clarity and urgency."
paras.zh: “记录变化已经不够了，”他们写道。 “我们还必须传达这意味着什么以及需要采取哪些行动。作为科学家，我们有责任清晰而紧迫地传达这些现实。”

paras.en: The authors include renowned climate experts: Michael Mann from the University of Pennsylvania, Sarah Perkins-Kirkpatrick of the Australian National University, Johan Rockström of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, and Anjal Prakash of FLAME University, among others.
paras.zh: 作者包括著名气候专家：宾夕法尼亚大学的迈克尔·曼、澳大利亚国立大学的莎拉·珀金斯-柯克帕特里克、波茨坦气候影响研究所的约翰·罗克斯特伦和火焰大学的安贾尔·普拉卡什等。

paras.en: Of 16 climate indicators the coalition tracks, seven have reached record extremes, the report finds, while several others also show troubling trends.
paras.zh: 报告发现，在该联盟追踪的 16 项气候指标中，有 7 项已达到创纪录的极端值，而其他几项也显示出令人不安的趋势。

paras.en: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, for example, exceeded 428 parts per million in May – higher than at any point in the last 2 million years.
paras.zh: 例如，5 月份大气中二氧化碳的浓度超过百万分之 428，高于过去 200 万年的任何时候。

paras.en: Rising CO2 levels are driven largely by humanity's CO2 emissions, which have also soared in recent centuries. Today's atmospheric CO2 is about 50 percent higher than it was in the late 18th century, before the Industrial Revolution, the report notes.
paras.zh: 二氧化碳水平上升主要是由人类二氧化碳排放量驱动的，近几个世纪以来人类二氧化碳排放量也在猛增。报告指出，当今大气中的二氧化碳含量比 18 世纪末工业革命之前的水平高出约 50%。

paras.en: Meanwhile, the rate of global warming appears to be speeding up, too, having risen from 0.19 degrees Celsius per decade between 1970 and 2010 to about 0.36 °C per decade since.
paras.zh: 与此同时，全球变暖的速度似乎也在加快，从 1970 年至 2010 年期间每十年升温 0.19 摄氏度上升至此后每十年约 0.36 摄氏度。

paras.en: Glacier thickness and Greenland ice mass have fallen to record lows, releasing surges of meltwater that, along with thermal expansion of seawater, are raising sea levels around the world.
paras.zh: 冰川厚度和格陵兰岛冰量已降至历史最低水平，释放出大量融水，再加上海水热膨胀，导致世界各地的海平面上升。

paras.en: Climate change is also boosting the risk of wildfire, which reduced global tree cover by 10.8 million hectares in 2025, the third-highest total on record. Since wildfires release greenhouse gases, this trend raises the specter of a dangerous feedback loop.
paras.zh: 气候变化还增加了野火的风险，导致 2025 年全球树木覆盖面积减少 1,080 万公顷，创有记录以来第三高。由于野火释放温室气体，这种趋势引发了危险反馈循环的担忧。

paras.en: And yet we're still digging deeper. Fossil fuel consumption increased by 0.9 percent in 2025, the authors report, with oil, coal, and natural gas all reaching record highs. Annual energy-related CO2 emissions also exceeded 41 gigatonnes for the first time, they note.
paras.zh: 然而我们仍在更深入地挖掘。作者报告称，到 2025 年，化石燃料消耗量将增加 0.9%，石油、煤炭和天然气均创下历史新高。他们指出，每年与能源相关的二氧化碳排放量也首次超过 41 十亿吨。

paras.en: "Many climate solutions are already technically feasible and increasingly cost competitive, but because climate change is driven by interconnected energy, economic, ecological and social systems, truly meaningful progress will likely depend on integrated responses across multiple sectors and scales," Ripple says.
paras.zh: “许多气候解决方案在技术上已经可行，而且成本竞争力越来越强，但由于气候变化是由相互关联的能源、经济、生态和社会系统驱动的，真正有意义的进展可能取决于跨多个部门和规模的综合应对措施，”里普尔说。

paras.en: Wind and solar power now provide increasingly viable alternatives, hinting at the dawn of a new clean-energy era in which fossil fuels quickly lose their luster.
paras.zh: 风能和太阳能现在提供了越来越可行的替代方案，暗示着新的清洁能源时代的到来，在这个时代，化石燃料很快失去了光彩。

paras.en: While that is encouraging, the researchers acknowledge, it's not enough.
paras.zh: 研究人员承认，虽然这令人鼓舞，但这还不够。

paras.en: "With low-carbon sources now providing about 43 percent of global electricity, we may be witnessing the emergence of what we call the 'Age of Electricity,'" says co-lead author Christopher Wolf, a data scientist at Terrestrial Ecosystems Research Associates.
paras.zh: “现在，低碳能源提供了全球约 43% 的电力，我们可能正在见证‘电力时代’的出现，”共同主要作者、陆地生态系统研究协会的数据科学家克里斯托弗·沃尔夫 (Christopher Wolf) 说道。

paras.en: "That is a reason for hope, but fossil fuel use and emissions are still at record levels, so the transition needs to accelerate dramatically."
paras.zh: “这是一个充满希望的理由，但化石燃料的使用和排放仍处于创纪录的水平，因此转型需要大幅加速。”

paras.en: That means not just chipping away at the mess we've made, but embracing clean energy the way previous generations went all-in on fossil fuels.
paras.zh: 这意味着不仅要消除我们造成的混乱，还要像前几代人全力使用化石燃料一样拥抱清洁能源。

paras.en: "Achieving the necessary emissions reductions and societal shifts at the speed and scale required depends on deep transformations in energy generation, consumption patterns, food systems, economic priorities, and governance structures, in ways that also promote biodiversity protection," Wolf says.
paras.zh: 沃尔夫说：“以所需的速度和规模实现必要的减排和社会转变取决于能源生产、消费模式、粮食系统、经济优先事项和治理结构的深刻转变，同时也促进生物多样性保护。”

paras.en: "Without those transformations, we won't be able to stabilize the climate system and reduce the risk of crossing dangerous Earth system tipping points."
paras.zh: “如果没有这些转变，我们将无法稳定气候系统并降低跨越危险的地球系统临界点的风险。”

paras.en: The research has been published in BioScience.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《生物科学》杂志上。

articles.title: Scientists Tested a Toad Venom Psychedelic on Treatment-Resistant Depression. Here's What Happened.
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: In a quest to improve patients' mental health, it seems scientists are working their way through a list of every psychedelic 'party' drug of the past century.
paras.zh: 为了改善患者的心理健康，科学家们似乎正在研究上个世纪每一种迷幻“派对”药物的清单。

paras.en: Ketamine, psilocybin, MDMA, LSD, and DMT have all become legitimate research drugs in recent decades, with some now established in certain countries as prescribed treatment options for cases of depression and other mental illnesses that don't improve with typical treatment.
paras.zh: 近几十年来，氯胺酮、赛洛西宾、MDMA、LSD 和 DMT 都已成为合法的研究药物，其中一些药物现已在某些国家被确定为抑郁症和其他精神疾病病例的处方治疗选择，这些疾病通过典型治疗无法改善。

paras.en: Now, a relatively obscure psychedelic compound based on toad venom is being investigated for its antidepressant potential. The results of a phase 2b randomized clinical trial have been published today in the Journal of the American Medical Association.
paras.zh: 现在，人们正在研究一种基于蟾蜍毒液的相对鲜为人知的迷幻化合物的抗抑郁潜力。 2b 期随机临床试验的结果已于今天发表在《美国医学会杂志》上。

paras.en: The trial, funded by biotech company AtaiBeckley (a subsidiary of pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly and Company), suggests a single-dose nasal spray formula of the substance could be a safe and speedy option for patients with difficult-to-treat depression.
paras.zh: 该试验由生物技术公司 AtaiBeckley（制药巨头礼来公司的子公司）资助，表明该物质的单剂量鼻喷雾配方可能是难以治疗的抑郁症患者的安全而快速的选择。

paras.en: The active ingredient is known as mebufotenin, or 5-MeO-DMT, and it originates from the Sonoran Desert toad (Incilius alvarius).
paras.zh: 该活性成分被称为美布福宁 (mebufotenin) 或 5-MeO-DMT，源自索诺兰沙漠蟾蜍 (Incilius alvarius)。

paras.en: It's one component of the notorious yet rare street drug 'bufo'. Usually sold as a dried form of the toad's actual venom, bufo contains both mebufotenin and bufotenin (5-HO-DMT).
paras.zh: 它是臭名昭著但罕见的街头毒品“bufo”的成分之一。蟾蜍通常以蟾蜍实际毒液的干燥形式出售，其中含有美蟾蜍毒素和蟾蜍毒素 (5-HO-DMT)。

paras.en: In the new clinical trial, however, researchers were testing a synthesized form of pure 5-MeO-DMT. It's not the first time this drug has gone through clinical trials – but it is the largest and most rigorous trial of it being used as a nasal spray yet.
paras.zh: 然而，在新的临床试验中，研究人员正在测试纯 5-MeO-DMT 的合成形式。这并不是这种药物第一次进行临床试验，但这是迄今为止规模最大、最严格的鼻喷雾剂试验。

paras.en: "Single-day dosing with mebufotenin appears to be effective for postpartum depression – and now for difficult-to-treat depression – and the benefits are sustained with or without retreatment for eight days to six months," explains psychopharmacology researcher Chittaranjan Andrade, of India's National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences.
paras.zh: 印度国家心理健康和神经科学研究所的精神药理学研究员 Chittaranjan Andrade 解释说：“单日服用美布福宁似乎对产后抑郁症有效，现在对难以治疗的抑郁症也有效，无论是否再次治疗，其益处都会持续八天到六个月。”

paras.en: Andrade was not involved in the new clinical trial, but has written an opinion piece on the research, also published in JAMA.
paras.zh: 安德拉德没有参与这项新的临床试验，但写了一篇关于该研究的评论文章，该文章也发表在《美国医学会杂志》上。

paras.en: Mebufotenin's unique mystical psychedelic effects kick in rapidly and subside within about an hour, with some variation depending on how the drug is taken. In that regard, it's similar to DMT, though the visual effects tend to be much less intense.
paras.zh: 美布福宁独特的神秘迷幻效果会迅速发挥作用，并在大约一个小时内消退，具体效果取决于药物的服用方式。在这方面，它与 DMT 类似，尽管视觉效果往往不那么强烈。

paras.en: Neuropsychiatry researcher David Feifel and colleagues think this rapid psychedelic experience could give mebufotenin an edge over options like esketamine and psilocybin, though the research isn't quite there yet.
paras.zh: 神经精神病学研究员 David Feifel 及其同事认为，这种快速的迷幻体验可能使美布福宁比艾氯胺酮和裸盖菇素等药物更具优势，尽管这项研究尚未完全实现。

paras.en: Their phase 2b clinical trial explores the drug's "safety, efficacy, and time to discharge readiness". The results are promising, but we're still a long way from seeing this Schedule 1/Class A drug in medical use outside research settings.
paras.zh: 他们的 2b 期临床试验探讨了该药物的“安全性、有效性和出院准备时间”。结果令人鼓舞，但我们距离看到这种 Schedule 1/A 类药物在研究环境之外的医疗用途还有很长的路要走。

paras.en: The trial included 193 participants undergoing treatment for moderate to severe major depression at institutions across Australia, Europe, and the US. They had tried two to five different antidepressant drugs during their current depressive episode, to no effect.
paras.zh: 该试验包括 193 名参与者，他们在澳大利亚、欧洲和美国的机构接受中度至重度抑郁症的治疗。在目前的抑郁发作期间，他们尝试了两到五种不同的抗抑郁药物，但没有效果。

paras.en: Each participant was randomly assigned a single dose of the mebufotenin benzoate nasal spray, containing either 0.3 mg, 8 mg, or 12 mg of the active substance, but to avoid bias, they were unaware of their dose.
paras.zh: 每个参与者被随机分配单剂量的苯甲酸美布福宁鼻喷雾剂，含有 0.3 毫克、8 毫克或 12 毫克活性物质，但为了避免偏差，他们不知道自己的剂量。

paras.en: They also received psychological support before, during, and after the 'trip', and followed protocols around set and setting typical of existing psychedelic treatments.
paras.zh: 他们还在“旅行”之前、期间和之后接受了心理支持，并遵循现有迷幻治疗典型的场景和设置协议。

paras.en: Most patients were ready to leave the treatment session within about two hours of taking the drug, after confirming they were no longer experiencing any acute psychedelic effects.
paras.zh: 大多数患者在确认不再经历任何急性迷幻作用后，在服药后约两小时内准备离开治疗。

paras.en: "This rapid return of dosed participants to baseline, together with infrequent dosing indicated by the long antidepressant durability after a single dose, can offer important potential advantages for patients and clinicians compared with treatment options currently available or in advanced stages of development," Feifel and team report.
paras.zh: Feifel 和团队报告说：“与目前可用或处于开发后期阶段的治疗方案相比，给药参与者快速恢复到基线，再加上单次给药后抗抑郁药持久耐用所表明的不频繁给药，可以为患者和临床医生提供重要的潜在优势。”

paras.en: "Esketamine and transcranial magnetic stimulation require frequent retreatment, and psilocybin and LSD require four to twelve hours of monitoring due to longer acute subjective effects."
paras.zh: “艾氯胺酮和经颅磁刺激需要频繁重新治疗，而裸盖菇素和 LSD 由于较长的急性主观影响而需要四到十二小时的监测。”

paras.en: Typically, patients started experiencing benefits about two days after the session, and these benefits continued for at least eight weeks.
paras.zh: 通常，患者在治疗后大约两天开始感受到益处，并且这些益处持续至少八周。

paras.en: The majority of patients experienced adverse side effects, but almost all of these were mild or moderate: things like headaches, nausea, and nasal pain, which quickly passed and occurred only on the day of dosing. However, one person experienced two severe panic attacks during their treatment.
paras.zh: 大多数患者都会出现不良副作用，但几乎所有这些副作用都是轻微或中度的：例如头痛、恶心和鼻痛，这些症状很快就会消失，并且仅在给药当天发生。然而，有一个人在治疗期间经历了两次严重的惊恐发作。

paras.en: The 12 mg and 8 mg doses both performed better than the 0.3 mg dose, improving depression scores by 5.3 and 6.2 more points than the lowest dose, respectively.
paras.zh: 12 mg 和 8 mg 剂量的表现均优于 0.3 mg 剂量，抑郁评分分别比最低剂量多改善 5.3 分和 6.2 分。

paras.en: The 8 mg dose will proceed to phase 3 since it seemed to produce the best balance of safety and efficacy. In phase 3, the drug will be tested on a much larger group of people and compared to other existing treatments.
paras.zh: 8 毫克剂量将进入第 3 阶段，因为它似乎能产生安全性和有效性的最佳平衡。在第三阶段，该药物将在更大的人群中进行测试，并与其他现有治疗方法进行比较。

paras.en: Andrade is not convinced these results bode well for mebufotenin as the next big thing in treating depression.
paras.zh: 安德拉德并不相信这些结果对于美布福宁作为治疗抑郁症的下一个重大药物来说是个好兆头。

paras.en: "The antidepressant effect was incomplete," he points out.
paras.zh: “抗抑郁效果并不完全，”他指出。

paras.en: "The average patient became only about 30 percent better, and the response and remission rates were below those typically seen, for example, with ketamine and electroconvulsive therapy."
paras.zh: “患者的平均病情仅好转 30% 左右，而且反应率和缓解率低于氯胺酮和电休克治疗等通常观察到的水平。”

paras.en: He also notes the study had a fairly lenient definition of 'treatment-resistant' depression: no patients had undergone ketamine or electroconvulsive therapy, for instance. 'Difficult-to-treat' depression is, in his eyes, a more accurate description of these patients.
paras.zh: 他还指出，该研究对“难治性”抑郁症的定义相当宽松：例如，没有患者接受过氯胺酮或电休克治疗。在他看来，“难治”抑郁症是对这些患者更准确的描述。

paras.en: The study also excluded any patients who reported suicidality, which means it's unclear how safe or effective mebufotenin would be for them.
paras.zh: 该研究还排除了任何报告有自杀倾向的患者，这意味着尚不清楚美布福宁对他们的安全性或有效性。

paras.en: He is also skeptical of the speed with which mebufotenin can really improve people's lives.
paras.zh: 他还对美布福宁能否真正改善人们的生活的速度持怀疑态度。

paras.en: "Patients with difficult-to-treat depression require long-term maintenance treatment, but because mebufotenin was examined as monotherapy, the trial
paras.zh: “患有难以治疗的抑郁症患者需要长期维持治疗，但由于美布福宁作为单一疗法进行了检查，该试验

paras.en: offers no insight on when and how the transition to a conventional antidepressant should be made or whether mebufotenin itself might be used for maintenance," he writes.
paras.zh: 没有提供关于何时以及如何过渡到传统抗抑郁药或美布福宁本身是否可以用于维持治疗的见解，”他写道。

paras.en: The research has been published in Journal of the American Medical Association.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《美国医学会杂志》上。

articles.title: Chinese scientists discover “D-rex,” a giant fungus with roots stretching back 65 million years

paras.en: Chinese scientists discover âD-rex,â a giant fungus with roots stretching back 65 million years
paras.zh: 中国科学家发现“D-rex”巨型真菌，其根部可追溯至 6500 万年前

paras.en: - Scientists have discovered a giant new fungus in China that grows up to 20 inches tall and weighs nearly five pounds, making it the largest known of its kind. Dubbed âD-rex,â its evolutionary lineage appears to have emerged shortly after the dinosaurs went extinct, raising intriguing questions about how that ancient catastrophe may have shaped its evolution.
paras.zh: - 科学家在中国发现了一种巨大的新真菌，它可以长到 20 英寸高，重近 5 磅，是已知的同类中最大的。它被称为“霸王龙”，它的进化谱系似乎是在恐龙灭绝后不久就出现的，这引发了关于这场古老的灾难可能如何影响它的进化的有趣问题。

paras.en: Scientists exploring the forests of Yunnan, China, have discovered an extraordinary giant fungus that is challenging previous assumptions about how large certain fungi can grow. The newly identified species, Dianjunus rex, produces upright reproductive structures that can reach 50 cm (20 inches) in height and weigh as much as 2.2 kg (4.9 pounds). These are the largest known fruiting bodies among fungi belonging to the phylum Ascomycota.
paras.zh: 探索中国云南森林的科学家发现了一种非凡的巨型真菌，它挑战了之前关于某些真菌可以生长到多大的假设。新发现的物种 Dianjunus rex 可产生直立的生殖结构，高度可达 50 厘米（20 英寸），重量可达 2.2 公斤（4.9 磅）。这些是子囊菌门真菌中已知最大的子实体。

paras.en: "This remarkable species represents a new fungal family, Dianjunaceae, and provides a rare window into the evolution of extreme fungal body forms," said Dr Indunil C Senanayake, an associate professor at the Germplasm Bank of Wild Species of the Kunming Institute of Botany in China and corresponding author of the study, published in Frontiers in Fungal Biology.
paras.zh: 中国昆明植物研究所野生物种种质库副教授、该研究的通讯作者Indunil C Senanayake博士说：“这个非凡的物种代表了一个新的真菌家族——电君子科，并为研究极端真菌体型的进化提供了一个难得的窗口。”该研究发表在《真菌生物学前沿》上。

paras.en: "The discovery illustrates how much fungus biodiversity remains to be discovered in East Asian forests."
paras.zh: “这一发现说明了东亚森林中还有多少真菌生物多样性有待发现。”

paras.en: A Giant Fungus Hidden in China's Forests
paras.zh: 隐藏在中国森林中的巨型真菌

paras.en: Researchers from the Kunming Institute of Botany encountered the unusual fungus while surveying several forest environments in Yunnan. Their fieldwork included temperate coniferous forests near Damaidi and Yipinglang, along with tropical rainforest near Nanbang.
paras.zh: 昆明植物研究所的研究人员在调查云南的几个森林环境时遇到了这种不寻常的真菌。他们的实地考察包括大麦地和一平廊附近的温带针叶林，以及南邦附近的热带雨林。

paras.en: The team spotted unusually large, whitish reproductive structures, known as 'stromata', growing from the woody roots of Chinese cork oak trees. These structures emerged from the rhizosphere, the region of soil surrounding plant roots, and appeared to belong to an unidentified member of the ascomycete fungi.
paras.zh: 研究小组发现了异常巨大的白色生殖结构，称为“基质”，从中国软木橡树的木质根部生长出来。这些结构出现在根际，即植物根部周围的土壤区域，似乎属于子囊菌的一个身份不明的成员。

paras.en: Ascomycetes make up the largest major group of fungi, with more than 64,000 recognized species. Unlike familiar mushrooms, these fungi do not produce true mushroom structures. Instead, they generate spores within tiny sac-like structures found inside or on the surfaces of their fruiting bodies.
paras.zh: 子囊菌是真菌中最大的主要类群，有超过 64,000 个已知物种。与熟悉的蘑菇不同，这些真菌不会产生真正的蘑菇结构。相反，它们在子实体内部或表面的微小囊状结构中产生孢子。

paras.en: To investigate the discovery, the scientists collected samples and preserved reference specimens in the Kunming Institute of Botany's collections. They also cultivated spores under laboratory conditions to examine the fungus's physical characteristics and sequenced its genome, including its protein-coding genes.
paras.zh: 为了研究这一发现，科学家们收集了样本，并在昆明植物研究所的收藏中保存了参考标本。他们还在实验室条件下培养孢子，以检查真菌的物理特征，并对其基因组进行测序，包括其蛋白质编码基因。

paras.en: Meet D-Rex, a Record-Breaking Fungal Giant
paras.zh: 来认识一下 D-Rex，一种破纪录的真菌巨人

paras.en: The genetic analysis, together with a close examination of the fungus's physical features, revealed that the discovery represented much more than a previously unknown species. It was sufficiently different from known fungi to require the creation of a new genus and an entirely new family (Dianjunaceae) within the order Xylariales.
